english: Before you stands an iron door.
At its center, a five-pointed star has been etched deep into the metal.
Esoteric energy emanates from the surface.
This door is sealed with powerful magic.
A faint hum vibrates through the iron.
That's some fancy door.
The star symbol... it's connected to something.
This is wizard work. Arcane and deliberate.
(Touch the door.)
(Examine the star symbol.)
Right, so...
Your gloved hand meets cold iron.
A ripple of translucent energy pulses across the surface.
It's locked. Magically.
Arcane Lock, just like at the tea shop.
But this one feels... stronger.
More personal.
You lean closer to inspect the etched star.
Five points. Perfectly symmetrical.
Five?
Obviously.
Four points. Perfectly symmetrical.
The work of a master craftsman. Or a wizard.
Probably both.
Each point of the star glows faintly with residual magic.
About your fancy mystery-dungeon-door?
He crosses his arms and stares at it.
Not really my area of expertise, Cleric.
But I'd bet you need some kind of password. Or a spell.
Or, you know...
He mimes breaking something with his fists.
Subtle. Very subtle.
But what he means here is violence.
But yeah. Could work.
Smash it.
Or perhaps, think for a bit.
Obviously, there should be a way to get inside.
You approach the iron door with the star symbol once more.
Still locked, I presume?
(Try the door handle.)
(Look for a keyhole.)
What kind of magic is sealing this?
Analyze the magical mechanics of the door.
Smash open the iron door.
(Press your ear against the door.)
I should ask the door to let me in.
E-Hm. Oh well. Maybe later.
You reach for the handle and pull.
Nothing. It doesn't budge.
Not even slightly.
You would require incredible power to break this seal.
GET. IT. DONE.
No. The door is completely sealed.
Hm. Too bad.
You search the door's surface carefully.
No keyhole. No lock mechanism visible at all.
This door doesn't open with a key.
It's purely magical.
Arcane Lock, without a doubt.
Powerful stuff. Higher level than most seals you've encountered.
Whoever placed this spell knew what they were doing.
The star is likely a focus point for the enchantment.
Can I dispel it?
Is there a password?
Could I break it down?
(Step back from the door.)
Dispel Magic could work, theoretically.
Obviously. If you had the spell for it.
But this seal feels particularly robust.
You'd need to be very skilled to break through.
Or very lucky.
Most Arcane Locks have passphrases.
A word or phrase that unseals the door instantly.
But you'd have to know what it is.
Guessing would be... difficult.
Especially with a wizard's seal. They tend to be creative.
No.
There might be passphrase however.
The door is iron. Thick iron.
Breaking through metal and magic...
That would require immense strength.
And the seal might fight back.
Magical wards often do.
You trace the etched lines of the star with your eyes.
The esoteric energy is strong, but the geometry is... imperfect.
The lower-left point of the star doesn't properly connect to the ward's anchoring matrix.
See something, Cleric?
If you apply blunt force at exactly a forty-five-degree angle to that specific point...
The kinetic energy will bypass the Arcane Lock's absorption field and shatter the iron underneath.
You know exactly where to strike.
You stare at the glowing star, trying to dissect the spellcraft.
The exact nature of the seal eludes you.
Get ready.
(Grab the door.)
You throw yourself against the iron.
Your muscles strain. Your body protests.
The door doesn't move. Not even a millimeter.
Instead, the star symbol flares bright blue.
A surge of electricity shoots through the iron.
(Take the blow.)
The shock travels up your arms and through your chest.
You stumble backward, smoke rising from your gloves.
That... was a mistake.
The door has defensive enchantments. Of course it does.
Shit. That even hit me a bit.
But good try, I guess.
Your hands are numb.
The tingling sensation spreads to your shoulders.
Note to self: don't try that again.
You think it was a wizard?
The star symbol. The seal. It's all wizard work.
Who else would seal a door this thoroughly?
Of course. Being a wizard myself, it's only natural I know what a wizard would wizard-think.
The goblin squints at you.
...Fair point.
Something valuable indeed.
Or something dangerous.
You lean close, listening.
Nothing. Complete silence.
The door is too thick. Or there's nothing beyond.
Or something is waiting very, very quietly.
Stop scaring yourself.
Yes. Obviously.
That's not- I mean it's...
It is an esoteric door, only esoteric methods will win out in the end.
(Clear your throat.)
Hm?
Prepare yourself.
Then speak.
TELL ME, <shake>OH DOOR</shake>, WHAT IS THY PASSPHRASE?!
Your companion is taken aback by the intense ejaculation.
Silence.
At first.
Then...
Are you trying a persuasion here, or...?
(Remain silent.)
He throws his hands up.
Master Hagginshags?
A tiny voice, faintly behind the iron door.
Not remember? Passphrase is: Learn! I will learn...!
Sorry, who is this?
THANK YOU, DOOR!
What? That actually worked?
Hm?
Oh no... not master at all!
The voice goes away.
Snell looks at you, then the door. Then you again.
Try it?
You quickly cast Grease on the mystery door.
Which does seem to work- although you're not sure by how much.
You channel every ounce of strength into your assault.
The iron door groans under the pressure.
Your muscles scream in protest.
The star symbol flickers and dims.
(One more push!)
With a deafening crack, the magical seal shatters.
Blue fragments of energy scatter like glass.
The door swings inward, defeated.
You did it. Through sheer brute force.
Holy shit.
You actually broke a wizard's seal with your bare hands.
He looks genuinely impressed.
Your arms feel like jelly.
Worth it.
The door swings open with a powerful boom.
The sound echoes through the dungeon hallways.
Everyone heard that.
Inside, you see a faint light emanating from within.
Soft. Almost inviting.
Or perhaps a trap. Probably a trap.
One locked door usually isn't enough for these fucking wizard types.
Well. After you, Cleric.
The goblin gestures toward the open doorway.
He's not going first, that's for sure.
Beyond lies the unknown.
What secrets did this wizard hide?
E-Time to find out.
